entwurf.titel_zeile1: From water pipes to Wall Street
entwurf.titel_zeile2: The 1799 bank that grew into the world’s largest
entwurf.beschreibung: JPMorgan Chase began as a New York water company in 1799, turned quickly into a bank, then merged with Chase and J.P. Morgan to dominate global finance.

teile.name: Hook
teile.text: Aaron Burr founded The Manhattan Company on September 1, 1799 to supply clean water to New York City.
teile.szene: A bustling 18th‑century New York street. Aaron Burr’s Manhattan Company opens, water pipes gleaming, early merchants trading goods under bright streetlamps.

teile.name: Background
teile.text: Within six months, the company opened a bank before any water pipes were laid.
teile.szene: A 2000s corporate boardroom. Executives from Chase and J.P. Morgan shake hands, papers signed, the skyline visible through glass.

teile.name: Obstacle
teile.text: In 2000, J.P. Morgan & Co. and Chase Manhattan Company merged to form JPMorgan Chase.
teile.szene: A dark, tense trading floor. Screens flash red numbers, traders in suits, emergency lights flicker.

teile.name: Response
teile.szene: A gleaming modern headquarters. Employees move through glass corridors, screens show rising stock charts.

teile.name: Consequence
teile.text: The merger brought retail banking, credit cards, and investment services under one roof.
teile.szene: An international cityscape at night, neon lights, a Chase bank sign glows.

teile.name: Call to action
teile.text: JPMorgan Chase now stands at 270 Park Avenue, the largest U.S. bank by market capitalization. Join us for more history. Like, share, and save if you enjoyed.
teile.szene: A friendly presenter in a studio, pointing to a like button on screen, bright lighting.
